Gboard UFC Flags: User Feature Cache, Touch Offsets and Speed

Read the APK evidence identifying UFC as User Feature Cache, and distinguish cached typing information from a supposed speed boost.

What you should know

UFC maps to User Feature Cache in the inspected GboardWu APK; the speed flag is not a general performance accelerator.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

What the APK actually calls UFC

Read-only analysis of GboardWu 18.5.4 identified package paths including com/google/android/libraries/inputmethod/userfeaturecache/guarder/UfcGuarder and UfcMetricsProcessorModule. These class names strongly support User Feature Cache as the expansion. They do not disclose every stored field or the persistence and export policy.

Interpret the three visible controls

enable_ufc_for_offset plausibly allows the decoder to use learned touch offsets. enable_ufc_for_speed plausibly uses a learned typing-speed signal rather than increasing processor speed. enable_export_ufc suggests an export path, but its destination and field contents are unverified. These are interpretations grounded in code context; individual runtime call-site outcomes have not been proven.

What not to infer

A paper on personalized keyboard geometry describes offset learning and measured decoder improvements, but it is not evidence that flipping the UFC switches yields those gains. An export toggle deserves caution because cached typing-related statistics can be sensitive. Avoid enabling diagnostics or dumping personal data simply to answer a curiosity.

Frequently asked questions

Does UFC make Gboard faster?

It may provide typing-speed information; the examined flag does not establish a performance boost.

What is in the UFC export?

The precise exported fields and destination are not documented by the evidence currently available to the Atlas.
